question.text: The number of enantiomers of the compound $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{CHBrCHBrCOOH}$ is

solution.text:
The structure $\mathrm{CH}_{3}{ }^{*} \mathrm{CH} \mathrm{Br} \mathrm{C}^{*} \mathrm{H} \mathrm{Br} \mathrm{COOH}$

has two different chiral carbon atoms, hence number of enantiomers (optically active forms) is $2^{n}=2^{2}=4$
